bull.b: Repaying the Coinbase facility removes a secured borrowing obligation and releases bitcoin, USDC, and cash collateral. This strengthens financing flexibility, reduces dependence on asset-backed debt, and gives Riot greater control over capital allocation as it funds data-center expansion.

The long-dated Rockdale lease adds contracted infrastructure revenue that is less dependent on Bitcoin mining conditions. Its 20-year term, expansion options, and targeted 80%–90% NOI margin could materially diversify Riot and support recurring earnings as capacity is delivered.

Low net power costs support mining competitiveness by improving the economics of deployed computing capacity. At the same time, stronger engineering revenue, margin expansion, and a $177.1 million backlog provide operational capabilities that can support data-center delivery and diversification.

bear.b: Severe losses show that current operations are not yet converting revenue into sustainable earnings. Although some quarterly charges were noncash, persistent negative EBIT, EBITDA, and net income reduce internal funding capacity and leave results highly sensitive to operating conditions and investment costs.

Ongoing operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean Riot is consuming capital while pursuing expansion rather than funding growth from operations. This raises reliance on financing and asset sales, potentially limiting flexibility if project spending remains high or operating results do not improve.

Riot’s largest growth opportunity requires substantial construction spending and project financing before the planned 2027–2028 deliveries generate rent. The scale of required capital increases execution and funding pressure, while debt-backed development can constrain flexibility if schedules or economics change.
